dedupe_keys.name: metro timetabling topology and simulated demand benchmark

description: The Train Timetabling authors publish a metro benchmark with topology, origin-destination matrices, model parameters and simulated time-varying station demand. The GitHub tree lists XLSX workbooks and small GTFS/AFC example CSVs. The data README attributes base experiment inputs to a 2023 INFORMS RAS competition. A separate README explains that observed fine-grained station demand was unavailable, so each station follows a synthetic 30–50–20 arrival split across three planning intervals. This is a line-scale test case, not a verified city-wide passenger survey. GitHub states MIT and the files are publicly accessible without cost, but the original competition input rights were not checked separately. A rail modeller could use the topology and demand tables to compare timetable, rolling-stock, skip-stop or queue-capacity scenarios. This review did not open workbook values or run optimization scripts. The root documentation names a reproducibility path that differs from the tree. Related resources include GTFS feeds and station-count data for replacing the synthetic demand.
licence: MIT (GitHub licence metadata and root LICENSE); original competition input rights were not separately checked.
